newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Senate leader steps aside.
newsitem.headline: Canada Senate leader steps aside.

text.p: Canada's Senate leader, Joyce Fairbairn, will step aside to make room in the new cabinet for someone from Nova Scotia, Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Wednesday.
Chretien is to name a new cabinet on Wednesday morning after his Liberal party was re-elected on June 2.

But Chretien has faced a dilemma in putting together the new cabinet. His party lost all its seats in the Atlantic province of Nova Scotia, leaving Chretien with no one to represent that area at the cabinet table.

In a letter to Chretien dated June 9, Fairbairn, from Alberta, said she was willing to step aside to allow a senator from Nova Scotia to become leader of the unelected senate and sit at the cabinet table.
She said she would remain a senator.
Chretien in a letter dated June 10 accepted her resignation as senate leader.
Without Fairbairn at the cabinet table, Alberta will likely be left with only one face in the cabinet: Anne McLellan, who is expected to move to the justice portfolio from natural resources.
